title: K-flatness is a triangulated property in the homotopy category
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] additive in each variable. Assume all small colimits exist [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and tensoring on either side with any fixed object preserves them. Use the direct-sum total tensor and two-sided K-flatness of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Write $K(A)$ for cochain complexes with maps modulo cochain homotopy, where $f-g=d h+h d$ for degree $-1$ maps $h$, and $q:\mathrm{CoCh}(A)\to K(A)$ for the quotient. For complexes, shifts and mapping cones use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. K-flatness is invariant under cochain homotopy equivalence, so the property $\mathcal P(qL)$ that $L$ is K-flat is well-defined and closed under isomorphisms in $K(A)$. The full subcategory defined by $\mathcal P$ contains zero, is stable under every integer shift, and contains the mapping cone of every map between its objects. Thus it is a triangulated full subcategory of $K(A)$; explicitly, in a triangle isomorphic to a mapping-cone triangle, if two vertices satisfy $\mathcal P$, then so does the third.

proof.text: Introduce the graded tensor compatibility instances by applying the assumed preservation of colimits to each of the coproduct diagrams in their definitions. Unfolding the two definitions identifies IsKFlatForTotalTensor of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] with (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)).kFlat: the tensorLeft and tensorRight maps are tensorHom with the identity in the fixed variable.

Apply the already proved upstream HomotopyCategory.kFlat_quotient_obj_iff (cited in the source and lean_audit of this node) in each direction. A HomotopyEquiv induces HomotopyCategory.isoOfHomotopyEquiv in the quotient category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; transport K-flatness along this isomorphism using ObjectProperty.prop_of_iso. This proves the first clause.

Identify the displayed existential object property with (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)).kFlat. In the forward direction transport quotient K-flatness along the inverse of the witnessing isomorphism. In the reverse direction choose a complex representative using quotient_obj_surjective, use the identity isomorphism, and apply kFlat_quotient_obj_iff. Rewrite by this equality and apply the already proved upstream IsTriangulated instance from WeilConjectures.FromJoel.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Flat.KFlat, which the source and lean_audit of this node already identify.

lean.statement: theorem kFlat_homotopy_isTriangulated {A : Type u} [Category.{v, u} A] [Abelian A] [MonoidalCategory A] [MonoidalPreadditive A] [HasColimits A] [∀ (X : A), PreservesColimits (tensorLeft X)] [∀ (X : A), PreservesColimits (tensorRight X)] : (∀ {L L' : CochainComplex A ℤ}, HomotopyEquiv L L' → L.IsKFlatForTotalTensor → L'.IsKFlatForTotalTensor) ∧ ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated (fun K : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ) => ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ), Nonempty (K ≅ (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj L) ∧ L.IsKFlatForTotalTensor)
lean.note: Second-reader fix (maintainer review): the delivered conclusion was only ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated of the isomorphism closure of q(K-flat complexes), which omits the node's clause that K-flatness is invariant under cochain homotopy equivalence (so P(qL) iff L is K-flat; upstream HomotopyCategory.kFlat_quotient_obj_iff). Added that clause as a first conjunct via Mathlib HomotopyEquiv; the triangulated conjunct and all hypotheses are unchanged. Docstrings now cite the node's source document lem-sfb-derived-monoidal.proof.md.
